notes: IBKR-focus tickers (local + common US listings). Scores are a first-pass judgment from public track records, investor discourse (X/letters), and classic serial-acquirer literature — not investment advice. Re-rank in the UI. 2026-11-11: added 38 established acquirers screened for proven CEOs and remaining runway; IBKR symbols follow the primary listing and should be confirmed in TWS.

companies.name: Constellation Software
companies.thesis: Gold standard VMS compounder. Thousands of small software acquisitions, extreme decentralization, owner-operator culture, ruthless capital hurdles.

developments.note: Continued high deal cadence across operating groups; Lumine/Topicus as related platforms in orbit.

companies.name: Amphenol
companies.thesis: Roughly 130 general managers run their own P&Ls with almost no HQ; acquired founders usually stay. Decades of bolt-ons across a still-fragmented connector/sensor market, now with an AI-datacenter tailwind. Deal sizes have stepped up sharply, which is the thing to watch.
sources: Fierce Network / Wirenet on CommScope + Trexon deals

developments.note: CommScope connectivity unit (~$10.5B, largest ever) followed by cable maker Trexon; management says it wants more M&A. Larger tickets test the 'many small deals' pillar.

companies.name: Waste Connections
companies.model: Decentralized waste roll-up in exclusive/secondary markets
companies.ceo: Ronald Mittelstaedt (founder; returned as CEO in 2023)
companies.thesis: Founder-led consolidator that targets exclusive franchise and secondary markets where it can be #1 or #2, then lets district managers own pricing and P&L. Highest margins and FCF conversion in the sector; private haulers still hold a large share of the market.

developments.note: 19 deals in 2025 (~$330M acquired annualized revenue), ~$125M of rollover revenue into 2026; ~$20M more closed in early February 2026.

companies.name: Danaher
companies.thesis: Best-in-class operating system (DBS) that makes 1+1>2 via process excellence and platform builds (e.g. bioprocessing). Larger deals than Swedish peers; still elite capital allocator.

developments.note: Portfolio reshaped toward life sciences/diagnostics; Cytiva integration as complete-solution example.

companies.name: Lifco
companies.thesis: Poster child of Swedish model: niche leaders, high autonomy, many small deals, dental + demolition + systems. Frequently cited as quality compounder.

developments.note: Investor focus on standards set by leadership; still a reference for newer Swedish acquirers.

companies.name: HEICO
companies.thesis: Buys niche aero/electronic businesses; FAA PMA parts + decentralization. Exceptional long-term returns; often compared with TransDigm.

developments.note: Buffett/Berkshire stake highlighted investor attention; rich valuation is the main constraint.

companies.name: FirstService
companies.ceo: Scott Patterson (CEO); founder Jay Hennick is Chairman
companies.thesis: Residential property management plus essential service brands (restoration, fire protection, roofing). Buys local operators as tuck-ins and keeps managers as equity partners. ~30 years of high-teens compounding from the Hennick lineage.

developments.note: Roofing Corp of America has become the newest tuck-in platform alongside Century Fire and First Onsite.

companies.name: AMETEK
companies.model: Niche instrument acquirer with operating system
companies.ceo: David Zapico (CEO since 2016; 35+ years at AMETEK)
companies.thesis: Two decades of buying niche differentiated instrument businesses and lifting margins with the AMETEK Growth Model. FCF conversion consistently above 100% of net income, almost all redeployed into M&A. A quieter Danaher/Roper.

developments.note: Agreed to buy Indicor Instrumentation for ~$5B — its largest deal by a wide margin. Bigger than the usual bolt-on; watch price paid and leverage.

companies.name: The Ensign Group
companies.ceo: Barry Port (CEO since 2019; 20+ years at Ensign)
companies.thesis: Buys underperforming skilled-nursing facilities cheaply and turns them around under local leaders who act as CEOs of their own building, grouped in peer clusters. One of the purest autonomy cultures in US public markets, with ~15,000 US facilities still mostly in small hands. Medicare/Medicaid reimbursement is the exogenous risk.

developments.note: Five more facilities (582 beds) brought the portfolio to 378 operations; 2026 guidance raised during the year.

companies.name: Watsco
companies.ceo: Albert Nahmad (Chairman & CEO since 1972); Aaron Nahmad is the heir apparent
companies.thesis: Largest US HVAC/R distributor, built by buying family distributors and leaving local leaders and brands in place. Near debt-free, restricted stock that vests at retirement, one of the best 30-year records on the NYSE. Now extending the playbook into plumbing.
sources: ACHR News, Digital Commerce 360 on Jackson Supply / Granite Group

developments.note: Agreed to buy The Granite Group (~$500M revenue plumbing/HVAC distributor, 82 locations) — a notable step into plumbing.
Completed Jackson Supply (Texas), adding Sunbelt density. Succession from Albert to Aaron Nahmad is the capital-allocator watch item.

companies.name: Arthur J. Gallagher
companies.ceo: J. Patrick Gallagher Jr. (Chairman & CEO; CEO since 1995)
companies.thesis: The most prolific tuck-in acquirer in insurance brokerage: dozens of small family-owned agencies a year at ~10-11x EBITDAC while the stock trades far higher. Thousands of independent brokers remain. AssuredPartners was an unusually large deal for them.

developments.note: Seven tuck-ins (~$63M annualized revenue) at ~11.3x EBITAC; 30+ term sheets (~$500M revenue) in the pipeline; deal pace ~80% of normal as sellers reset price expectations. Organic growth 6%.
AssuredPartners (~$13.5B) integration on plan: $160M run-rate synergies targeted by end-2026, up to $325M by early 2028.

companies.name: TerraVest Industries
companies.ceo: Dustin Haw (CEO); Charles Pellerin is Executive Chairman
companies.thesis: Buys dull manufacturers (propane tanks, boilers, trailers) at 4-6x EBITDA from founders, keeps them decentralized, and invests in plant efficiency. Insiders own a lot; one of the best-performing Canadian stocks of the past decade. Energy exposure and larger recent deals add risk.

developments.note: Added KBK Industries, Superior Pressure Vessels and B&R Repair after the larger EnTrans deal in 2025.

companies.name: Vitec Software Group
companies.thesis: The Nordic answer to Constellation: ~40 years of buying profitable niche vertical software companies in the Nordics and Benelux and holding them forever in autonomous units. Mostly recurring revenue; uses modest debt and occasional share issues, unlike CSU.

developments.note: Acquired Autonet (January) and AtermIT (October); issued SEK 700M of senior notes to fund the pipeline.

companies.name: TransDigm
companies.thesis: Acquires proprietary aerospace components with pricing power; aggressive capital structure and value extraction post-close.

companies.name: Addtech
companies.thesis: Long IPO compounding history (~179x cited at Redeye conference). Niche tech trading companies, autonomy culture.

companies.name: Lagercrantz
companies.thesis: High-quality Swedish compounder; often ranked near Addtech/Lifco for consistency of small niche deals.

companies.name: Halma
companies.thesis: CSU-like autonomy in safety/health niches; small critical businesses with regulation/mission-critical demand.

companies.name: Topicus.com
companies.thesis: European VMS spin/platform in Constellation orbit. Frequently in serial-acquirer portfolios for 2025+.

companies.name: Investment AB Latour
companies.model: Douglas-family holdco with wholly owned serial acquirers
companies.ceo: Johan Hjertonsson (CEO since 2019); Douglas family controls
companies.thesis: Two engines: wholly owned industrial groups (Swegon, Hultafors, Nord-Lock, Caljan) that each do bolt-ons, and long-held listed stakes (Assa Abloy, Sweco, Tomra). ~40 years of market-beating returns with low costs. Usually trades at a premium to NAV.

developments.note: Acquired LaminAir, strengthening its position in Switzerland.

companies.name: Comfort Systems USA
companies.thesis: Buys well-run local mechanical and electrical contractors at mid-single-digit multiples and leaves them alone — names, leaders and P&Ls stay. Net cash balance sheet, buybacks, and a data-center/modular boom on top. Cyclicality of construction is the main risk.
sources: Comfort Systems FY2025 10-K / Q4 call coverage

developments.note: Record backlog driven by technology/data-center work; continues adding one to three operating companies a year.

companies.name: CRH
companies.thesis: Does 20-40 bolt-ons a year, mostly family-owned quarries and paving businesses that cannot be replicated, and actively recycles the portfolio. US listing since 2023 and federal infrastructure spending support the story. Arcosa is far larger than its usual deal.
sources: Business Wire / Financier Worldwide on Arcosa

developments.note: Agreed to buy Arcosa for $8.5B all-cash — its biggest deal ever, adding US aggregates and infrastructure products.

companies.name: TFI International
companies.thesis: Bédard has done 200+ deals, buying unloved trucking assets cheaply (UPS Freight for $800M is the classic), stripping bad freight and running each unit for free cash flow. Aggressive buybacks when M&A is quiet. Cyclical, and his succession is the key question.

developments.note: Still doing small tuck-ins (tanker carrier, Fleetway) through a weak freight market; has said no large deal near term.

companies.name: Rollins
companies.ceo: Jerry Gahlhoff Jr. (CEO since 2023); Rollins family controls
companies.thesis: Orkin parent; recurring, recession-resistant route business that buys dozens of local pest operators a year plus an occasional regional brand. Asset-light with negative working capital; the industry still has ~17,000+ small US operators.

developments.note: 99th consecutive quarter of revenue growth. Saela (2025) and Fox (2023) are the recent regional brand deals alongside routine tuck-ins.

companies.name: Richelieu Hardware
companies.thesis: Lord has run the same playbook for 35+ years: several small distributor acquisitions every year, no meaningful debt, steady US expansion. Slow and steady rather than spectacular; margins have been under pressure post-pandemic.

developments.note: Three Canadian acquisitions mid-year plus The Penrod Company (US$70M sales); Q3 sales +12.6%.

companies.name: Kelly Partners Group
companies.ceo: Brett Kelly (founder, Executive Chairman & CEO; owns ~half)
companies.thesis: Buys 51% of small accounting firms at ~4-5x and leaves partners owning 49% — an explicit Berkshire/Constellation-inspired system. Tens of thousands of target firms across Australia, the US and UK. Small and thinly traded, uses meaningful debt, and is very dependent on its founder.

developments.note: FY2026 revenue +18% to ~A$159M as US/UK expansion continues; exploring an additional overseas listing.

companies.name: Colliers International
companies.industry: Real Estate Services / Engineering / Investment Mgmt
companies.thesis: Hennick has compounded at roughly 20% a year for three decades using the same recipe: buy professional-services firms, leave operators with meaningful equity. Colliers has diversified from brokerage into engineering and investment management, both with long tuck-in runways.

developments.note: Engineering segment continues to add firms; recurring revenue now the majority of earnings.

companies.name: Descartes Systems
companies.thesis: Has bought 60+ small logistics and trade-compliance software businesses and plugged them into its Global Logistics Network. Funded entirely from cash flow, net cash balance sheet, ~45% adjusted EBITDA margins.

developments.note: Acquired Idelic (fleet safety, ~$25M) and Drivin, after Extensiv (~$120M).

companies.name: Kingspan Group
companies.thesis: Three decades of acquisitions have built the global leader in insulated panels, now expanding into roofing, data-centre solutions and natural insulation. Decentralized divisions, family ownership, and a record of buying counter-cyclically.

developments.note: Forecasting a sharp rise in 2026 trading profit on data-centre demand.
Paused its €650M buyback to keep dry powder for deals; agreed to buy data-centre power specialist BMC Manufacturing (~€850M).

companies.name: Momentum Group
companies.thesis: Spun out of Alligo in 2022 and culturally from the Bergman & Beving tree. Buys small Nordic industrial component and service specialists; high returns on working capital (the P/WC discipline) and a long list of small targets.

developments.note: Q2 flagged 'high acquisition activity'; Q3 showed robust earnings growth in a gradually improving market.

companies.name: DSV
companies.ceo: Jens Lund (CEO since 2024; previously long-time CFO/COO)
companies.thesis: The best large-deal integrator in Europe: UTi, Panalpina, Agility GIL and now Schenker each moved onto one IT platform with margins lifted to DSV levels. Few, large deals rather than many small ones, and after Schenker it is the world's #1 forwarder, so M&A runway is limited — the return driver is integration plus buybacks.

developments.note: Schenker integration progressing on plan with H1 2026 earnings growth; buybacks expected to resume as leverage falls.

companies.name: CCL Industries
companies.thesis: World's largest label maker. Martin's record includes Avery, Checkpoint and Innovia bought at low multiples and fixed, plus a steady stream of small plant-level bolt-ons. Conservative balance sheet, Lang family control.

developments.note: Closed Sleever International and agreed to buy ALT Technologies for CCL Design.

companies.name: Volution Group
companies.thesis: Buys local ventilation brands across the UK, Europe and Australasia and keeps them as brands while sharing sourcing and motors. Regulation on energy efficiency and indoor air quality drives demand; ~20%+ operating margins and strong cash conversion.

developments.note: FY2026 revenue +15.7% with adjusted operating margin of 23.2%; completed AC Industries in Australia following Fantech.

companies.name: Roper Technologies
companies.thesis: Shifted toward software/network niches; pays up more than Swedish peers but strong cash conversion and capital allocation culture.

companies.name: Indutrade
companies.thesis: Large, established Swedish industrial acquirer with broad niche portfolio and decentralization DNA.

companies.name: Judges Scientific
companies.thesis: Long ROIIC track record (~20% cited) buying scientific instrument niches; favorite of UK small-cap compounder investors.

developments.note: Geotek integration watched as a test of model scaling.

companies.name: Diploma
companies.thesis: Specialist distributors/controls; steady bolt-ons with disciplined culture.

companies.name: Rokosgruppen (Roko)
companies.thesis: Younger Swedish platform; investors like risk/reward vs mature peers. Leadership transition is the live watch item.

developments.note: CEO transition (Karlsson → Bladh) flagged as capital-allocator stress test.

companies.name: Teqnion
companies.thesis: Smaller/younger Swedish acquirer often owned by dedicated compounder investors for upside vs Lifco/Addtech.

companies.name: CSW Industrials
companies.ceo: Joseph Armes (Chairman & CEO since the 2015 spin-off)
companies.thesis: Buys small, high-margin branded consumables and parts (RectorSeal lineage) and pushes them through its HVAC/plumbing distribution reach. Returns and margins have risen steadily under Armes; low leverage historically.

developments.note: Stepped up deal size with Aspen Manufacturing and MARS Parts in 2025; another $25.8M deployed in Contractor Solutions in March 2026.

companies.name: Thermo Fisher Scientific
companies.thesis: Casper has deployed well over $50B on acquisitions (Life Technologies, Patheon, PPD) while compounding EPS in the mid-teens. Scale and the PPI system make 1+1>2 real, but deals are large and fully priced — a Danaher-style platform builder, not a multiple-arbitrage story.

developments.note: Completed Clario (clinical-trial endpoint data, ~$9B) after buying Solventum's purification & filtration unit in 2025.

companies.name: RBC Bearings
companies.thesis: Hartnett has built RBC from a small bearing maker through 30 years of acquisitions of sole-source engineered components, with the highest margins in the bearing industry. Deals are occasional rather than programmatic (Dodge 2021, VACCO 2025) and he is in his late 70s.

developments.note: Bought VACCO Industries from ESCO for $310M, deepening space/defense exposure.

companies.name: WSP Global
companies.thesis: Grew from a Quebec regional firm (Genivar) into one of the world's largest pure-play engineering consultancies via 150+ acquisitions. People business with low capital needs; the sector is still fragmented. Deals are getting bigger and are partly equity-funded.
sources: WSP / La Caisse releases on TRC

developments.note: Bought TRC (US$3.3B) to lead in power & energy; record ~$19.7B backlog; management openly hunting more multibillion-dollar targets.

companies.name: Lumine Group
companies.thesis: Communications/media software verticals; Constellation DNA. Earlier-stage than CSU/Topicus.

companies.name: Teledyne Technologies
companies.thesis: Long history of tech/instrumentation M&A; Outsiders-adjacent capital allocation culture.

companies.name: Illinois Tool Works
companies.thesis: More organic/80-20 than pure roll-up, but excellent capital allocation and selective M&A; often grouped with compounders.

companies.name: United Rentals
companies.thesis: Classic cost/density synergy roll-up (branch network). Brad Jacobs lineage DNA; more integrated than Swedish autonomy model.
sources: How to Make a Few Billion Dollars

companies.name: Atlas Copco
companies.thesis: Global industrial champion with continuous small acquisitions and decentralized structure; quality over pure multiple arbitrage.

companies.name: Loar Holdings
companies.thesis: Founded in 2012 on the TransDigm playbook: proprietary, sole-source aerospace components with heavy aftermarket, bought from founders and small PE funds. Much smaller than TDG/HEI so each deal moves the needle; listed only since 2024 and richly valued.

developments.note: Closed Harper Engineering (~$250M); record Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 with 2026 outlook raised twice.

companies.name: APi Group
companies.ceo: Russ Becker (CEO since 2002); Sir Martin Franklin & James Lillie co-chair
companies.thesis: World's largest fire & life-safety services provider. Statutorily required inspections pull through higher-margin service work, and thousands of local fire/security contractors remain to buy. Chubb (2022) was the one transformative deal; since then it has been steady bolt-ons.

developments.note: Closed CertaSite, Onyx-Fire Protection and Evergreen Fire and Security; raised 2026 guidance after Onyx.

companies.name: Ryan Specialty
companies.ceo: Patrick G. Ryan (founder of Aon; Executive Chairman) with Timothy Turner as CEO
companies.thesis: Pat Ryan's second act: the leading E&S wholesale broker and MGU platform, rolling up specialty underwriting businesses as risk migrates to the E&S market. Pays more per deal than retail brokers; founder owns a large stake.

developments.note: Announced a restructuring program alongside continued revenue growth; watch organic growth as E&S property pricing softens.

companies.name: Sika
companies.ceo: Thomas Hasler (CEO since 2021; 30+ years at Sika)
companies.thesis: Global leader in construction chemicals that adds several local bolt-ons every year in a still-fragmented market, plus the occasional platform (MBCC, Parex). Strong local-manager culture. Growth has slowed with China and European construction.

developments.note: Raised 2026 growth outlook after H1 following a profit drop in 2025; Investor Day put adhesives at the centre of strategy.

companies.name: Tyler Technologies
companies.thesis: Dominant US local-government software vendor, built over 25 years by acquiring niche public-sector products and cross-selling into a sticky installed base. More integrated and pricier than the CSU model, but very long cloud-migration and payments runway.

developments.note: Acquired CloudGavel (electronic warrants) — typical small product tuck-in.

companies.name: IMCD
companies.thesis: Asset-light distributor of specialty chemicals and food/pharma ingredients that has done 100+ acquisitions of local distributors worldwide. Long runway, but organic growth has been weak, the CEO changed abruptly in 2025 and the stock has de-rated — the new leadership still has to prove itself.

developments.note: H1 2026 showed revenue and profit growth again after a soft 2025.

companies.name: Sdiptech
companies.thesis: Buys niche product companies tied to infrastructure upgrades (water, energy efficiency, safety) with high margins. Deals rely heavily on earn-outs, which muddies cash conversion, and the stock has de-rated sharply — more of a value-priced Swedish acquirer than a proven elite one.

developments.note: CEO change to Anders Mattson; acquisition pace slowed while leverage and earn-out liabilities are worked down.

companies.name: Beijer Ref
companies.thesis: The Watsco of the rest of the world: consolidating refrigeration and HVAC wholesalers across Europe, APAC and, since 2023, the US. Long runway, EQT as anchor owner. Working capital is heavy and the CEO seat has just turned over, so it does not yet meet the 'proven CEO' test.

developments.note: Christopher Norbye stepped down in August; Joel Davidsson was acting CEO until Jonas Steen's appointment. Deals continued (North American HVAC distributor, Airstream in Australia).

companies.name: SHIFT Inc.
companies.thesis: Founder-led software-testing leader that buys small, sub-scale Japanese IT firms at low multiples (succession-driven sellers) and lifts utilisation and engineer pay. Huge fragmented market, but lower margins and a more execution-heavy model than Western VMS acquirers.

developments.note: Set up an investment fund to accelerate M&A and merged subsidiaries to simplify the group; FY2025 results were boosted by acquisitions.

companies.name: Assa Abloy
companies.thesis: Decades of door/access consolidations worldwide; more scale synergy than micro-niche autonomy.

companies.name: Addnode Group
companies.thesis: Swedish software/engineering digitalization acquirer in the Add* family ecosystem.

companies.name: Boyd Group Services
companies.thesis: Largest non-franchised collision repair operator in North America with a ~30-year record of single-shop and small-chain acquisitions in a market of 30,000+ shops. Margins have disappointed since 2020 and the CEO is new, so this is a turnaround within a roll-up.

developments.note: Closed Joe Hudson's Collision Center (US$1.3B) — its largest deal — alongside a US listing and equity raise.

companies.name: QXO
companies.ceo: Brad Jacobs (Chairman & CEO; built United Rentals, XPO, GXO, RXO)
companies.thesis: Jacobs' sixth roll-up, aimed at the ~$800B fragmented building-products distribution market with a $50B revenue goal. The CEO is as proven as they come, but this is the opposite of the Swedish model: few, very large, equity-funded deals with heavy integration. A bet on the jockey.

developments.note: Completed the ~$17B TopBuild acquisition after buying Kodiak Building Partners for $2.25B in February; revenue run-rate now well above $16B.
Beacon Roofing Supply (~$11B) was the platform deal.

companies.name: AddLife
companies.thesis: Life science product companies; Swedish autonomy model with more cyclical/medtech exposure.

companies.name: Bergman & Beving
companies.thesis: Grandfather of the Swedish model (spinoffs created enormous value). Smaller today but culturally important.

companies.name: Bufab
companies.thesis: Strong 10yr returns among Swedish cowboys; niche industrial supply chain roll-ups.

companies.name: Interpump Group
companies.thesis: Buys niche hydraulics at ~4–8x; redeploys ~50% FCF; limited leverage. Underfollowed vs Nordics.

companies.name: Brown & Brown
companies.thesis: Long-running US insurance broker consolidator; appears on dedicated serial-acquirer portfolios.

companies.name: SS&C Technologies
companies.thesis: Large-scale software/fintech M&A; Andvari note on ownership incentives is useful context.

companies.name: Ashtead Group
companies.thesis: Scale rental consolidator via Sunbelt; cyclical and more synergy/density driven.

companies.name: Alimentation Couche-Tard
companies.thesis: Proven large-scale retail consolidator; bigger deals and integration-heavy vs niche autonomy model.

companies.name: Vitalhub
companies.thesis: Smaller Canadian healthcare software consolidator; runway attractive, track record still seasoning.

companies.name: Chapters Group
companies.thesis: Emerging European software compounder; overlaps with Judges/Software Circle talent network.

companies.name: Software Circle
companies.thesis: Early-innings UK VMS roll-up with Judges/Chapters-related board DNA; speculative but on-framework.

companies.name: Renew Holdings
companies.thesis: Under-the-radar UK serial acquirer in engineering services (cited alongside Judges).

companies.name: Berkshire Hathaway
companies.thesis: Ultimate capital allocator; fewer 'roll-up' deals today but the philosophical north star for autonomy + capital allocation.

companies.name: LVMH
companies.thesis: Acquires and stewards luxury brands; different economics than industrial/VMS roll-ups but fits acquisitive compounder set.

companies.name: Enghouse Systems
companies.thesis: Canadian software acquirer; useful foil/competitor context vs Constellation orbit (Drive interview notes).

companies.name: Bunzl
companies.thesis: Steady distribution consolidator; less 'sexy' than VMS/Swedish names but durable deal machine.
